sources.title: Jane Addams, Twenty Years at Hull-House, with Autobiographical Notes (1910)

proactive_agency.rationale: Co-founded Hull House with Ellen Gates Starr in 1889, one of the first settlement houses in the US, a specific, dated, self-initiated founding act with no institutional mandate behind it.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Publicly opposed US entry into WWI, a documented, controversial position at the time that cost her significant public standing (she was labeled unpatriotic by some contemporaries), yet she sustained her pacifist advocacy through the war and afterward.

leadership_drive.rationale: Helped found and chaired the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom, inferred as sustained leadership drive from the documented founding and chairing role.

persistence.rationale: Sustained her pacifist advocacy through WWI's duration and its unpopular political cost, and continued Hull House's operation for over four decades until her death, inferred as real persistence from the documented duration of both commitments.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustaining a publicly unpopular pacifist stance through the war years implies real tolerance for sustained public disapproval, inferred from the documented reputational cost of her position at the time.

collaboration.rationale: Was a founding member of both the NAACP and the ACLU alongside other prominent contemporaries, suggesting real sustained collaborative capacity across multiple organizations, inferred from the documented range of her co-founding roles.

achievement_drive.rationale: Sustained organizational founding and leadership across sociology, social work, and peace activism over four decades implies strong achievement drive, inferred from the documented breadth of her founded initiatives.

analytical_rigor.rationale: Her sustained sociological writing on urban poverty and immigration, informed directly by Hull House's documented work, suggests real analytical engagement with her subject matter.

discipline.rationale: Sustaining Hull House's operation and her own writing output over four decades implies real behavioral discipline, inferred from the documented length of her involvement.

impact_motivation.rationale: A sustained, multi-decade career oriented toward social reform and peace advocacy, culminating in the 1931 Nobel Peace Prize, implies strong impact motivation, inferred from the documented consistency of her life's work.

independent_thinking.rationale: Sustaining a publicly unpopular pacifist position through WWI, against the prevailing patriotic consensus of the time, suggests real independent judgment, inferred from the documented reputational cost she accepted.

curiosity.rationale: Sustained sociological writing on urban poverty, immigration, and social reform across four decades suggests broad intellectual curiosity about her social environment, inferred from the documented range of her published subjects.

detail_orientation.rationale: Managing Hull House's sustained day-to-day operation across four decades, alongside detailed sociological documentation of its surrounding neighborhood, implies real attention to organizational and observational detail.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Sustained public speaking, fundraising, and organizing across four decades implies real social assertiveness, inferred from the documented scale of Hull House's public profile.

planning_orientation.rationale: Building and sustaining Hull House's expanding programs (education, healthcare, arts) over decades implies real methodical institutional planning, inferred from the documented growth of the institution.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Sustained, increasingly influential sociological and organizational work over four decades suggests developing mastery, inferred from the documented career arc culminating in the Nobel Peace Prize.

adaptability.rationale: Successfully sustaining Hull House and her advocacy work through major shifts in American political climate (Progressive Era through WWI and its aftermath) implies real adaptability, inferred from the documented institutional continuity across these periods.

autonomy_need.rationale: Founding an independent institution outside any existing charitable or religious organizational structure suggests real self-direction, inferred from the documented independent founding of Hull House.
